name: Trysil

seo.title: Trysil ski resort guide
seo.description: Norway's largest ski resort: 41 lifts and 71 slopes over four interconnected areas, with 685 metres of vertical on one SkiPass.
seo.twitterDescription: 41 lifts, 71 slopes, four interconnected areas, 685 m of vertical.
seo.webpageDescription: Ski facts, slopes by grade per area, where to stay and how to get to Trysil in Innlandet, Norway.

h1: Trysil ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Trysil is a single cone of a mountain skied from four sides, and all four are on one SkiPass: Turistsenteret with the gondola and the adventure pool, Skihytta in the sun, Høyfjellsenteret high up, and Högegga where the steep slopes and the tree skiing are. Forty-one lifts serve 71 slopes over 685 metres of vertical.

kpis.label: Vertical drop
kpis.note: four linked areas on one SkiPass

stayOverview: The four areas ring one mountain, so the side you sleep on decides your first run rather than your whole week. Turistsenteret is the biggest and has the gondola; Högegga is the steep side; Skihytta and Høyfjellsenteret sit between them.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. All four areas connect on the mountain, so the choice is about the walk to the lift and what you want at the end of the day.
rentalCars: A car helps for moving between the four bases at valley level, though the mountain connects them all on skis.

sources.label: SkiStar: Trysil lifts, slopes and weather

travelTips.title: Which side
travelTips.text: Turistsenteret has 16 of its 23 slopes graded very easy or easy; Högegga has 8 difficult of 13. They are opposite ends of the same mountain.
travelTips.sourceLabel: SkiStar: Trysil lifts, slopes and weather

travelTips.title: Two countries, one pass
travelTips.text: A SkiPass of three days or more in Trysil includes two days in Sälen across the Swedish border.

travelTips.title: The gondola
travelTips.text: Trysil's gondola runs from Turistsenteret, the largest of the four areas.

highlights.title: Högegga
highlights.text: Trysil's steepest side: 8 of its 13 slopes are graded difficult, with tree skiing and an express lift.
highlights.sourceLabel: SkiStar: Trysil lifts, slopes and weather

highlights.title: Turistsenteret
highlights.text: The largest area, with the gondola, an adventure pool, a spa and a large children's area.

highlights.title: Skihytta
highlights.text: The sunny side, with an express lift, a children's area and ski-in ski-out cabins.

highlights.title: Høyfjellsenteret
highlights.text: The high-mountain area, with ski school, rental and the SkiStar Lodge.

areas.name: Turistsenteret
areas.text: Trysil's largest area, with the gondola, shops, restaurants, an adventure pool and a spa.

areas.name: Skihytta
areas.text: Express lift, restaurant and children's area, with ski-in ski-out cabins.

areas.name: Høyfjellsenteret
areas.text: Family-friendly high-mountain area with ski school, rental and the SkiStar Lodge.
areas.bestFor: high terrain, ski school, SkiStar Lodge

areas.name: Högegga
areas.text: Trysil's steepest slopes and its tree skiing, with an express lift onto the rest of the mountain.
areas.bestFor: steep slopes, tree skiing, experienced skiers

topElevation.unannounced: SkiStar publishes the vertical drop but no summit elevation for Trysil, also not on the rendered slopes page.

season.note: Turistsenteret opens first on 4 December; Høyfjellssenteret follows 12 December and Högegga and Skihytta 18 December, all closing 18 April. The operator's season-opening page gives the same start.
season.sourceLabel: SkiStar Trysil: lift opening hours, season 2026/27

longestRun.unannounced: The operator gives 71 slopes, 41 lifts and 685 m of vertical across four linked areas, but publishes no run lengths and names no longest run.

dayPass.unannounced: SkiStar prices the SkiPass by booking date and states it is cheapest the earlier it is booked, so there is no fixed adult day rate.

facts.label: Four linked areas
facts.value: Turistsenteret, Skihytta, Høyfjellsenteret and Högegga on one SkiPass

facts.text: Turistsenteret has 16 of its 23 slopes graded very easy or easy, plus a large children's area, an adventure pool and a spa.
facts.sourceLabel: SkiStar: Trysil lifts, slopes and weather

facts.text: Skihytta has a children's area and cabins with ski-in ski-out access.
Högegga has 8 difficult slopes of 13 - more black runs than the other two charted areas together - with tree skiing and the resort's steepest terrain.
facts.sourceLabel: SkiStar: Trysil lifts, slopes and weather

unannounced.statement: SkiStar does not publish a fixed adult day rate: the SkiPass is priced by booking date, and the operator states it is cheapest the earlier it is booked.
SkiStar's slope page breaks out Turistsenteret, Skihytta and Högegga but not Høyfjellsenteret, so 22 of the 71 slopes have no published grade split.
unannounced.sourceLabel: SkiStar: Trysil lifts, slopes and weather

pisteDistribution.label: Slopes by grade, per ski area
pisteDistribution.note: SkiStar breaks out three of Trysil's four areas on its slope page. Høyfjellsenteret is not among them, so these rows cover 49 of the resort's 71 slopes.
pisteDistribution.sourceLabel: SkiStar: Trysil lifts, slopes and weather
